history.dynasty: Legendary Treta Yuga origins; modern redevelopment
history.period: Treta Yuga (legendary); redevelopment foundation stone 13 December 2023 (Nitish Kumar); Rs 882.87 crore redevelopment announced 2025, completion expected ~2027 (Bhumi Pujan for redevelopment project by Amit Shah, 8 August 2025)
history.summary: Punaura Dham, 5 km southwest of Sitamarhi city, is revered in the Ramayana tradition as the birthplace of Sita - the field where King Janaka's plough unearthed the infant Sita during a famine, beside the ashram of the Vedic sage Pundrik (from which the name Punaura is said to derive). One of the few temples where Sita is worshipped independently, it is a Government of India cultural-heritage site and a key Ramayana Circuit destination. Behind the Sita temple lies Janaki Kund (Wikipedia coordinates 26.586453 N, 85.466757 E), whose waters are believed to bless childless couples. Since 2019 the Mahavir Mandir Trust runs a free Sita Rasoi here. CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column holds the town name 'Sitamarhi'; the real state is Bihar. Coordinates are approximate (taken from the documented Sita Kund location).

name: Punaura Dham Temple
town_description: Punaura is a village about 5 km southwest of Sitamarhi city in the Mithila region of north Bihar, near the India-Nepal border. It is best known as Punaura Dham, the revered birthplace of Goddess Sita, drawing lakhs of pilgrims annually and now being redeveloped with a grand Sita temple and pilgrim corridor.

travel.road: Sitamarhi Bus Stand, about 4.5 km; daily bus service from Punaura Dham to Haleshwar Sthan, Panthpakar and Janakpur (Nepal) run by Mahavir Mandir Trust
